_about: Settings > Connectors (projects/everyday/CONNECTORS.md, E55): one row per connector the reach bundle holds, minus arm-remind and arm-browser (they reach no outside account). kind: reach = reaches the person from another app, arm = lets the agent read or call an outside app. secret: the name of the saved secret it reads (Settings > Secrets), or null. two_way: talks back into the Hive; never offered an On here (warden ruling 1105030716fe). can_finish_here: pasting the secret is the whole setup. unit: the systemd user unit that runs it, without .service (a timer keeps .timer), or null when nothing runs (the agent calls it when asked). conn-webhooks' unit is written with \u escapes because the reach bundle names it with this project's old short name, and the export renames that word everywhere else. shared: another part of the Hive reads the same secret (Telnyx's key is the phone line's too), so the paste box warns, and hides once that secret is saved. needs: what the person has to bring, and the step left when it can't be finished here.

connectors.name: arm-calendar
connectors.label: Calendar
connectors.line: Lets the agent read today's and the next events from a private calendar link. Nothing writes to the calendar.
connectors.needs: Your calendar's private ICS link: paste it here.

connectors.name: arm-homeassistant
connectors.label: Home Assistant
connectors.line: Lets the agent read your home's states and call only the services you list.
connectors.needs: A long-lived token from your Home Assistant, pasted here, then an agent or a terminal writes the list of allowed services.

connectors.name: arm-watch
connectors.label: Feeds and pages
connectors.line: Lets the agent watch RSS feeds and web pages and post what changed.
connectors.needs: Nothing from you. Ask an agent to watch a feed or page.

connectors.name: arm-hook
connectors.label: Outgoing webhooks
connectors.line: Lets the agent send a short message to a web address you approved.
connectors.needs: The address to send to. An agent or a terminal adds it to the approved list.

connectors.name: conn-webhooks
connectors.label: Incoming webhooks
connectors.line: Receives signed webhooks on this computer and posts them to a conversation, marked as outside data.
connectors.needs: A config file with each sender's key, written by an agent or in a terminal.

connectors.name: conn-ntfy
connectors.label: ntfy
connectors.line: Pushes a short note to your phone when something waits for you.
connectors.needs: The ntfy app on your phone. Set it up in Phone alerts.

connectors.name: conn-webpush
connectors.label: Web push
connectors.line: Notifies this browser or your phone when the app is closed.
connectors.needs: Nothing else. Set it up in Push notifications.

connectors.name: conn-gotify
connectors.label: Gotify
connectors.line: Pushes a short note to your phone through your own Gotify server.
connectors.needs: An app token from your Gotify server, pasted here, then an agent or a terminal sets the server's address.

connectors.name: conn-teams
connectors.label: Microsoft Teams
connectors.line: Posts a short note into a Teams channel. It can't read anything back.
connectors.needs: A Workflows webhook address you made in Teams, pasted here, then an agent or a terminal turns it on.

connectors.name: conn-googlechat
connectors.label: Google Chat
connectors.line: Posts a short note into a Google Chat space. It can't read anything back.
connectors.needs: An incoming webhook address you made in the space, pasted here, then an agent or a terminal turns it on.

connectors.name: conn-sms
connectors.label: Text messages
connectors.line: Texts your own phone through Telnyx. Send only.
connectors.needs: A Telnyx account and its API key, then an agent or a terminal sets your number and turns it on.

connectors.name: conn-telegram
connectors.label: Telegram
connectors.line: Talk to the Hive from Telegram through a bot of yours.
connectors.needs: A Telegram bot of your own.

connectors.name: conn-discord
connectors.label: Discord
connectors.line: Talk to the Hive from Discord direct messages through a bot of yours.
connectors.needs: A Discord bot of your own.

connectors.name: conn-signal
connectors.label: Signal
connectors.line: Talk to the Hive from Signal's Note to Self.
connectors.needs: Your Signal account, linked as a device.

connectors.name: conn-whatsapp
connectors.label: WhatsApp
connectors.line: Talk to the Hive from WhatsApp's Message Yourself chat.
connectors.needs: Your WhatsApp account, linked as a device.

connectors.name: conn-imessage
connectors.label: iMessage
connectors.line: Talk to the Hive from iMessage's chat with yourself.
connectors.needs: A Mac of yours running a small script.

connectors.name: conn-email
connectors.label: Email
connectors.line: Talk to the Hive by email, through a mailbox of its own.
connectors.needs: A separate mailbox for the Hive.

connectors.name: conn-matrix
connectors.label: Matrix
connectors.line: Talk to the Hive from Matrix through a bot account of yours.
connectors.needs: A bot account on a Matrix server.

connectors.name: conn-mattermost
connectors.label: Mattermost
connectors.line: Talk to the Hive from Mattermost direct messages.
connectors.needs: A bot on a Mattermost server.

connectors.name: conn-nextcloud
connectors.label: Nextcloud Talk
connectors.line: Talk to the Hive from Nextcloud Talk one-to-one chats.
connectors.needs: An app password on a Nextcloud server.

connectors.name: conn-rocketchat
connectors.label: Rocket.Chat
connectors.line: Talk to the Hive from Rocket.Chat direct messages.
connectors.needs: A bot or user token on a Rocket.Chat server.

connectors.name: conn-zulip
connectors.label: Zulip
connectors.line: Talk to the Hive from Zulip private messages.
connectors.needs: A bot on a Zulip server.

connectors.name: conn-xmpp
connectors.label: XMPP
connectors.line: Talk to the Hive over XMPP one-to-one chats.
connectors.needs: An account on an XMPP server.

connectors.name: conn-irc
connectors.label: IRC
connectors.line: Talk to the Hive over IRC private messages.
connectors.needs: An account on an IRC network.
